claims.text: Systematically varying elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr will produce measurable local changes in mechanical properties.
Changing the composition of HfNbTaTiZr will produce measurable changes in hardness.
Increasing Hf or Ta content can increase hardness.
The proposed hardness increase from Hf or Ta arises from enhanced lattice distortion.
The proposed hardness increase from Hf or Ta arises from bonding effects.
Combinatorial materials synthesis can create HfNbTaTiZr composition spreads with systematically varied elemental percentages.
Nanoindentation mapping can assess local mechanical properties across the HfNbTaTiZr composition spreads.
Local elemental-composition variations affect phase distribution.
Local elemental-composition variations affect grain structures.
Local elemental-composition variations affect bonding environments.
Changing the relative percentages of the constituent elements modifies local lattice distortions.
Changing the relative percentages of the constituent elements modifies local bonding networks.
Changes in lattice distortion and bonding networks alter resistance to deformation.
Hf- or Ta-enriched regions will have higher hardness than Ti- or Zr-enriched regions.
Composition–property maps will show systematic correlations between composition and measured mechanical properties.
Mechanical properties of standard equiatomic or near-equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr have been reported in previous studies.
Nonlinear interactions among constituent elements could complicate attribution of mechanical-property changes to individual elements.
